User palettes for the visual-report house style, round 2

Each column renders the same sample in one palette: answer box, section header, table with a highlighted cell, inline code, code panel, DAG nodes, chart series and the two semantic callouts. Fonts follow variant B. The strip under each name is the supplied palette verbatim; colours that fail as text are used only as fills or lines, and their darker same-hue text variants are listed under "Derived colours". Paper is B's #fbfbf9, the supplied white, or the brand paper. Every text pair passes WCAG AA (4.5:1) and every graphic pair 3:1; the ratio table sits under each column.

Note. Exactly one commit followed 088a29f; the source said three.

  • Signal #B4552D vs problem red: problems use crimson #a8182f with a cross icon. Signal is 4.20:1 on paper, so it is fills and lines only; accent text is signal-text #A34D29 (4.92).
  • Brand muted #6B675C (4.83) and label #6F6B60 (4.55) pass on paper. Label fails on hair #DFDCD4 (3.88), so labels never sit on hair.
  • Ochre series #A0832A is close to the amber note colour: flagged, kept because it is a brand value.
  • #5F91C1 (sequential/ordinal step 3) is 2.85:1 on paper: fills next to other steps only, not a standalone line. Pale #7FA6C9 (2.19) is fill-only.
  • Code family: the brand blue (#15619D on #dde8f3), apart from the burnt-orange signal.
